name: dbportal
description: Shared database portal for SRE, DevOps and developers: central datasources, SSO, and an audit trail of every execution.
//trustedDependencies: Explicit allowlist of the ONLY dependencies permitted to execute code at install time. Without this field bun applies its own default allowlist, which synthesizes a `node-gyp rebuild` for any package shipping a binding.gyp - including better-sqlite3 13, whose `gypfile: false` says not to (it is N-API and ships prebuilts, so npm honours it and bun does not). These three are exactly the packages that ran scripts before the field existed; cpu-features (optional, ssh2) and unrs-resolver stay blocked as they already were.
//overrides: Transitive dependencies held above what their parent's range would otherwise resolve to; `bun audit` is the check, and every entry here should be re-checked whenever its parent moves. lodash: recharts asks for ^4.17.21 and CVE-2026-4800 (arbitrary code execution via untrusted input in template imports) is fixed in 4.18.0; inside the parent's range, so this only forces resolution forward. Nothing here imports lodash directly. adm-zip: cassandra-driver asks for ~0.5.10; CVE-2026-39244 (denial of service through a crafted ZIP) is fixed in 0.6.0 and GHSA-vwc7-r8mq-g2x9 (extraction follows destination symlinks) in 0.6.1, both OUTSIDE that range. The path is not reachable from this product - adm-zip's one consumer in the driver, lib/datastax/cloud/index.js, returns from init() unless a `cloud` option (Astra secure-connect bundles) is set, which no connection here sets - but the pin is taken rather than argued away; 0.6.0 was verified against a live Apache Cassandra 5.0.9. undici: @workflow/world-local and @workflow/world-vercel pin 7.28.0 exactly; GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272 (cross-user cache disclosure) and four moderate advisories are fixed in 7.29.0. @ai-sdk/provider-utils already resolves ^7.28.0 to 7.29.1, so this dedupes to the one patched copy. nanoid: @workflow/core pins 5.1.6 exactly; GHSA-28wg-ghj8-5hjv and GHSA-xwg4-73v4-xw9w (integer overflow, infinite loop on a negative size) are fixed in 5.1.16. Bun applies an override to every occurrence of the name, so postcss (which asks for ^3.3.18) gets nanoid 5 too: it is ESM-only, and postcss loads `nanoid/non-secure` with require(), which Node 26 resolves through require(esm) - verified by the build. Drop this entry once @workflow/core raises its own floor. dompurify: monaco-editor pins 3.4.8 exactly; GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7 (IN_PLACE hook removal leaves a detached subtree executable) and three others are fixed by 3.4.12. A patch-level bump of the sanitizer monaco uses for hover markdown; the editor was checked by hand after the bump.

scripts.test: bun test tests/unit tests/api tests/integration && bun test tests/hooks && bun test tests/security && bun test tests/evals && bun run test:components
scripts.test:integration:postgres: bun test tests/integration/routes/postgres-routes.test.ts && bun test tests/integration/storage/postgres-audit-partitions.test.ts && bun test tests/integration/db/virtual-provider.test.ts
scripts.test:coverage: rm -rf coverage && bun run test:coverage:core && bun run test:components:coverage && node scripts/merge-lcov.mjs coverage/core/file-*/lcov.info coverage/components/lcov.info coverage/lcov.info
scripts.test:coverage-html:
bun run test:coverage && genhtml coverage/lcov.info --output-directory coverage/html && echo '
 Open coverage/html/index.html in your browser'

//dependencies: @duckdb/node-api is the one exact pin in this list. Its versions carry a prerelease suffix (1.5.5-r.4 = DuckDB 1.5.5, driver revision 4), and npm and bun treat a caret over a prerelease tag inconsistently - `^1.5.5-r.4` would resolve forward across 1.x in a way neither tool agrees on - so the range is written out. The driver is four packages, not one: @duckdb/node-api -> @duckdb/node-bindings -> a per-platform, per-libc @duckdb/node-bindings-<platform>-<arch>[-musl] holding duckdb.node next to the ~70 MB libduckdb.so it links against. None of the four declares a scripts block or a binding.gyp, so no trustedDependencies entry is needed. Bumping it is a provider change, not a routine bump (see docs/providers/duckdb.md and the tri-sync rule in CLAUDE.md).
